questions.h: What type is a / b when both are int, before the result is stored?
questions.e: a / b is integer division (3) before it is stored in the double, so c is 3.0, which cout prints as 3.

questions.q: Which of these is a char literal?
questions.h: Single quotes hold exactly one character.
questions.e: Single quotes make one character. "A" is a string, A is a variable name, and 'AB' is not a single character.

questions.h: A long long is 64 bits. How many bytes is that?
questions.e: A long long takes 8 bytes (64 bits).

questions.h: An unsigned int can't be negative. What happens when it goes below 0?
questions.e: unsigned int can't be negative. Going below 0 wraps around to the largest value, 4,294,967,295.

questions.h: Look up the ASCII codes of 'a' and 'A'.
questions.e: 'a' is 97 and 'A' is 65, so the difference is 32: lowercase = uppercase + 32.

questions.q: Which reads a whole line, spaces included, into string s?
questions.h: cin >> stops at the first space.
questions.e: cin >> stops at the first space. getline reads up to the end of the line.

questions.h: Do the steps in order: +=, then *=, then %=.
fixed with setprecision(2) rounds to 2 decimal places.
questions.e: 2 / 3 = 0.666…, and setprecision(2) with fixed rounds it to 2 decimal places: 0.67.

questions.q: An int can hold numbers up to about:
questions.h: An int has 32 bits, and one of them is the sign.
questions.e: A 32-bit int goes up to 2,147,483,647. 9.2 × 10^18 is long long, and 4.3 × 10^9 is unsigned int.

questions.h: Any non-zero value stored in a bool becomes true. What is true as a number?
questions.e: Any non-zero value stored in a bool becomes true (1), and true is 1, so 1 + 1 = 2.
